sanskrit: iheta devīr ayam astu panthā ayaṃ vo lokaḥ śaraṇāya sādhuḥ | idaṃ havir juṣamāṇā udeta kṣiprā rājñā varuṇena prasūtāḥ ||
english: Come hither, O divine ones; let this be the path; this world is good for your shelter. Rise up, enjoying this oblation; swiftly, urged on by King Varuṇa.

sanskrit: ihaitu rājā varuṇo 'jirābhir devo devībhir haviṣo juṣāṇaḥ | kṛṇuṣva panthām udayānam ūrmibhir anena babhro mahatā pṛthivyāḥ ||
english: Let King Varuṇa come hither with his swift ones, the god together with the goddesses, taking delight in the oblation. Make for yourself an ascending path with the waves — O tawny one — by means of this great earth.

sanskrit: priye dhriyadhvam udayānam undatīr oka aughānām iha rāraṇītu | anena vegān asṛjat prajāpatir iha dhriyadhvaṃ śaraṇaṃ sarasvatīḥ ||
english: O dear ones, hold fast to the ascending way; let the flooding waters rejoice here in their home among the floods. Prajāpati released the currents through this; O Sarasvatīs, hold fast here as refuge.

sanskrit: iha vo jūtir dhriyatāṃ samāny apām agnīnāṃ varuṇasya soma | anena vegān asṛjat tviṣīmato 'hiṃsrāñ chambhūn ajirām̐ atṛṣṇajaḥ ||
english: Let your common impulse be held here — of the waters, of the fires, of Varuṇa, of Soma. Through this one, the resplendent one released the currents — harmless, auspicious, swift — the one free from thirst.

sanskrit: ye pārato madhyato ye te antayor apsuṣado nihitās tīre agnayaḥ | te devajā iha no mṛḍayantv āpaś ca janmann ubhaye sabandhavaḥ ||
english: The fires that are placed beyond, in the middle, and at the two ends — seated in the waters, established on the bank — may those born of the gods be gracious to us here; and the waters too, both kinsmen from birth.

sanskrit: idaṃ va āpo hṛdayam ayaṃ vatsa ṛtāvarīḥ | ihettham eta śakvarīr yatremam̐ veśayāmasi ||
english: This is your heart, O waters, O mighty ones rich in truth; this is your calf. Come hither thus, O powerful ones, to where we settle this one.

sanskrit: ud asau sūryo agād ud ayaṃ māmako bhagaḥ | tenāhaṃ vidvalā patim abhy asākṣi viṣāsahiḥ ||
english: Yonder Sūrya has risen; my good fortune has risen too. Thereby have I, the knowing one, overcome my husband — victorious and prevailing.

sanskrit: ahaṃ ketur ahaṃ mūrdhā- -aham ugrā vivācanī | mamed api kratuṃ patiḥ sehānāyā upā carāt ||
english: I am the banner; I am the head; I am the fierce, commanding one. My husband shall attend upon my will, yielding to me who bear up under all.

sanskrit: mama putrāḥ śatruhaṇo 'tho me duhitā virāṭ | utāham asmi saṃjayā patyāṃ me śloka uttamaḥ ||
english: My sons are slayers of enemies; my daughter too is a sovereign ruler. And I myself am the victorious one; my glory over my husband is supreme.

sanskrit: yena devā asurebhyo 'bhavan dyumnavattarāḥ | idaṃ tad akri devā asapatnā kilābhuvam ||
english: By that whereby the gods became more glorious than the Asuras — by that, O gods, was this done; I have become free of rivals.

sanskrit: asapatnā sapatnaghnī jayanty abhibhūvarī | muṣṇāmy anyāsāṃ bhagaṃ vāso astheyasām iva ||
english: Without rivals, a slayer of rivals, victorious, overpowering — I steal the fortune of the other women as one strips the garment of one with no firm standing.

sanskrit: śerabhaka śerabha | punar vo yantu yātavaḥ punar jūtiḥ kimīdinaḥ | yasya stha tam atta yo vaḥ prāhait tam atta svā māṃsāny atta ||
english: O śerabhaka, O śerabha! Let the Yātu-demons go back again; let the rushing Kimīdin-demons go back again. Devour him to whom you belong; devour him who dispatched you; eat your own flesh.
O śevṛdhaka, O śevṛdha! [Formula repeated as in 2.42.1: Let the Yātu-demons go back; let the Kimīdin-demons go back; devour him to whom you belong; devour him who dispatched you; eat your own flesh.]
O sarpānusarpa! [Formula repeated as in 2.42.1: Let the Yātu-demons go back; let the Kimīdin-demons go back; devour him to whom you belong; devour him who dispatched you; eat your own flesh.]
O mrokānumroka! [Formula repeated as in 2.42.1: Let the Yātu-demons go back; let the Kimīdin-demons go back; devour him to whom you belong; devour him who dispatched you; eat your own flesh.]

sanskrit: jūrṇa bharūjy arjuny upabdo | punar vo yantu yātavaḥ punar jūtiḥ kimīdinaḥ | yasya stha tam atta yo vaḥ prāhait tam atta svā māṃsāny atta ||
english: O Jūrṇa, Bharūji, Arjuni, Upabda! Let the Yātu-demons go back again; let the rushing Kimīdin-demons go back again. Devour him to whom you belong; devour him who dispatched you; eat your own flesh.
